title: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Calling an exhausting shift flexible does not give the worker back their night.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side asks who pays for respectable explanations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its distinctive test follows the burden, even when an institution serves a real purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book connects public authority, emotional resilience, and algorithmic decisions through that question.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks readers to separate necessary cooperation from costs made difficult to challenge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a bakery calling its new night rota an efficiency improvement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bread still needs to reach the shop each morning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But the same baker now carries more of the disrupted sleep.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Management's label cannot tell us whether that distribution is necessary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book's burden test asks who benefits, who bears costs, and who can object.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some constraints are real; their current allocation still needs justification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The emotional chapters ask what happens when resilience replaces a response to exhaustion.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Support can help someone face pressure without making that pressure acceptable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In our example, a calmer conversation leaves the night rota unchanged.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AI could intensify this distance when a score appears to make the decision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also asks whether automation could remove some degrading work instead.
